TL;DR: KV-Control introduces a novel interface for precise control in text-conditioned 3D human motion synthesis, allowing for trajectory adherence without sacrificing motion quality.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the limitations in existing methods that either compromise on precision or involve cumbersome testing processes when incorporating trajectories and constraints in text-conditioned motion synthesis.

Method: KV-Control utilizes a memory-based interface within self-attention layers of frozen masked transformers, incorporating geometric constraints as controllable memory, alongside the part-tokenized motion substrate (PartVQ) and T-Concat.

Result: The method enables sub-centimeter accuracy in tracking constraints and effectively maintains the quality of text-conditioned generated motions, while only adding a minimal number of trainable parameters.

Conclusion: KV-Control effectively reframes the challenge of trajectory conditioning in text-to-motion generation, resulting in a system that is lightweight, precise, and offers clear control.

Abstract: Text-conditioned 3D human motion models now synthesize plausible motions from prompts, but practical animation and embodied-agent workflows rarely stop at text: a character may need to follow a sketched root path, hit an end-effector target, or satisfy a multi-joint trajectory while still preserving the gait, style, and intent described by language. This exposes a control trade-off. A trajectory controller should be precise without overwriting the pretrained text-conditioned motion prior, yet existing solutions either duplicate large portions of the generator to regain per-layer control access or move much of the cost to test-time optimization. We introduce KV-Control, a compact attention-side control interface for frozen masked text-to-motion transformers. The key idea is to make geometric constraints available as memory inside self-attention rather than injecting them through a global pose token or enforcing them only at the output side. To support this interface, we co-design a part-tokenized motion substrate and controller: \textbf{PartVQ} learns anatomy-aligned part codebooks, T-Concat exposes each frame--part token as an attention-addressable site, and KV-Control injects control-conditioned key/value memories at every self-attention layer while preserving the pretrained query stream, text cross-attention, FFN, and all backbone weights. The resulting adapter adds only trainable injection parameters atop a shared trajectory encoder, yet tracks root and multi-joint constraints with sub-centimeter accuracy under the inherited refinement protocol while retaining text-conditioned motion quality. KV-Control reframes trajectory conditioning as lightweight memory retrieval, providing a small, precise, and transparent control interface for text-to-motion generation.

</details>


### [31] [ShotCrop$^3$: Cropping Human-Centric Images into Cinematic Triple-Shot Compositions](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05635)
*Dehong Kong,Lina Lei,Lingtao Zheng,Chenyang Wu,Ailing Zhang,Xinran Qin,Teng Ma,Jiaqi Xu,Zhixin Wang,Zhikai Chen,Xuecheng Qi,Renjing Pei,Fan Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper introduces Triple-Shot Compositions (TSC), a novel task generating three-shot sets from single images for improved visual storytelling in creative workflows, developing the ShotCrop model with advanced training techniques and benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the inadequacy of existing methods that focus solely on single aesthetically pleasing crops, acknowledging the importance of multiple shots in narrative-driven creative processes, such as commercial posters.

Method: The authors propose the ShotCrop model, leveraging a three-stage training process involving Chain-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning, semi-supervised fine-tuning with pseudo labeling, and Group Relative Policy Optimization with a tailored composite reward.

Result: ShotCrop significantly outperforms GPT-5 in shot localization accuracy, achieving an average improvement of 2.82 times, and establishes TSC-Bench with 1.2k expert-annotated test cases for evaluation.

Conclusion: The integration of multiple shots enhances narrative value, demonstrating the effectiveness of the ShotCrop model in advancing multi-shot composition tasks.

Abstract: Prior work on aesthetic composition typically produces a single aesthetically pleasing crop, overlooking the narrative value of composing multiple shots from one scene. In practice, multi-shot composition is critical for downstream creative workflows: commercial posters often require multiple crops with different emphases (e.g., context, subject, and emotion/product details) to present key story beats. Therefore, we propose \textbf{Triple-Shot Compositions (TSC)}, a composition task that generates a three-shot set -- establishing, medium, and close-up -- from a single human-centric image, each paired with a brief shot description to support visual narration. To learn TSC with limited expert annotations, we introduce \textbf{ShotCrop} which undergoes a three-stage training process: it first applies Chain-of-Thought supervised fine-tuning to establish basic reasoning and aesthetic shot-cropping skills, then performs semi-supervised fine-tuning with high-confidence pseudo labels to further enhance aesthetic capability, and is finally optimized with Group Relative Policy Optimization for \textbf{ShotCrop} (GRPO-S) using a composite reward tailored for it. Specifically, our pseudo-labeling strategy combines MLLM-based scoring, aesthetic assessment, and CLIP similarity to retain high-confidence training signals. In addition, we present TSC-Bench, a benchmark of 1.2k expert-annotated test cases. Notably, ShotCrop achieves an average improvement of \textbf{2.82} times over GPT-5 in shot localization accuracy.

</details>


### [32] [Multi-Task Crack Foundation Model for Engineering-Reliable Crack Representation and Topology Preservation in Civil Infrastructure](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05641)
*Blessing Agyei Kyem,Joshua Kofi Asamoah,Eugene Denteh,Armstrong Aboah*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CrackGeoFM, a multi-task framework, improves crack assessment by integrating advanced modules for mask prediction, skeleton reconstruction, and uncertainty estimation, achieving state-of-the-art results across various datasets.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Reliable crack assessment requires accurately segmented cracks with stable confidence estimates, which is often lacking in existing models due to segmentation fragmentation and uncertainty issues.

Method: CrackGeoFM utilizes a frozen backbone with tailored adaptations, introducing components like FCEM, CFAM, and SMTD for enhanced mask prediction, topology preservation, and uncertainty calibration.

Result: The framework achieves state-of-the-art segmentation, better topology preservation, calibrated uncertainty, and effective adaptation with minimal labeled data across 20 crack datasets.

Conclusion: CrackGeoFM enables reliable and generalizable crack analysis, making it suitable for engineering applications in infrastructure assessment.

Abstract: Reliable crack assessment requires not only accurate pixel-level masks but also connected crack geometry and confidence estimates that remain stable under domain shift. However, existing segmentation models can achieve high overlap scores while fragmenting cracks, missing fine branches, and providing no calibrated uncertainty. To address this gap, this paper proposes CrackGeoFM, a multi-task framework that combines a frozen visual foundation backbone with crack-specific adaptation for mask prediction, skeleton reconstruction, and uncertainty estimation. The framework integrates a Frequency-Guided Crack Enhancement Module (FCEM) to enhance high-frequency crack cues, a Crack-Domain Feature Adaptation Module (CFAM) to adapt frozen backbone features to crack-domain patterns, and a Structure-Aware Multi-Task Decoder (SMTD) to jointly decode masks, skeletons, and uncertainty. Across 20 crack datasets, CrackGeoFM achieves state-of-the-art segmentation, improved topology preservation, calibrated uncertainty, and effective few-shot adaptation with only five labeled images. These results support reliable, generalizable, and engineering-oriented crack analysis for infrastructure assessment.

</details>


### [33] [CoFi-UCGen: Coarse-to-Fine Unsupervised Conditional Generation without Label Priors](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05652)
*Shengxi Li,Zhaokun Hu,Ce Zheng,Mai Xu,Jingyuan Xia,Si Liu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CoFi-UCGen is a novel framework for unsupervised conditional image generation that effectively disentangles global semantics and fine-grained variations without relying on labels.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The need for improved unsupervised conditional image generation that manages unstructured semantic representations.

Method: The framework incorporates adversarial semantic reciprocal learning to maintain consistency between images and latent spaces, utilizes bit-codes for a structured latent space, and introduces hierarchical modulation in diffusion models.

Result: CoFi-UCGen outperforms existing methods in image quality, semantic consistency, and control accuracy without label priors or pre-trained extractors.

Conclusion: The framework's successes validate the importance of coarse-to-fine semantic decomposition in addressing challenges in unsupervised conditional image generation.

Abstract: Unsupervised conditional image generation (UCGen) aims to control generation without relying on manually annotated labels, yet remains challenging due to unstructured semantic representations across granularities. To address this, we propose a novel coarse-to-fine UCGen framework (CoFi-UCGen) that explicitly disentangles global semantics from fine-grained variations, which to the best of our knowledge, sets out the first successful attempt for both coarse- and fine-grained conditional generation without any labels. More specifically, we first propose the adversarial semantic reciprocal learning theory to ensure the semantic consistency and completeness between images and latent spaces. Based on the consistency, we propose the bit-codes to learn a structured coarse-grained latent space, and further prove distinct global semantics inherent from our bit-codes while preserving independent noise sampling for generation. Building upon these bit-codes, we establish a fine-grained semantic basis and introduce a hierarchical modulation mechanism in diffusion models, by enabling layer-wise injection from coarse conditions to progressively control fine-grained attributes during generation. Extensive experiments demonstrate that without any label priors or pre-trained feature extractors, our CoFi-UCGen consistently outperforms existing UCGen methods in terms of image quality, semantic consistency, and control accuracy, verifying the effectiveness of explicit coarse-to-fine semantic decomposition for the challenging UCGen task.

</details>


### [34] [V2V-Bench: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Video-to-Video Generation Evaluation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05665)
*Tao Liu,Leela Krishna,Gouti Pavan Kumar,Sreeja K,Vishav Garg*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: V2V-Bench is a new benchmark for evaluating video-to-video generation, focusing on critical dimensions such as alignment and quality, while demonstrating strong correlation with human evaluations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the limitations in existing metrics for evaluating video-to-video generation that fail to capture editing instructions and frame correspondence.

Method: Introduction of V2V-Bench, a benchmark comprising 11 dimensions across five categories to evaluate V2V models, paired with diverse videos and editing tasks.

Result: Evaluation of Grok Imagine and Gemini Veo3 (commercial models) alongside Open Sora 2 (open-source model) demonstrated varying strengths; Grok excelled in editing fidelity, Veo3 in visual quality.

Conclusion: V2V-Bench achieved a high Spearman correlation of 0.905 with human judgments on six dimensions, indicating its effectiveness in evaluating V2V generation quality.

Abstract: Video-to-video (V2V) generation is difficult to evaluate because outputs must both follow editing instructions and preserve frame-level correspondence with the source video, which existing T2V and I2V metrics do not capture. We introduce V2V-Bench, a 11-dimension benchmark organized into five categories: temporal alignment, structural fidelity, transformation quality, video quality, and semantic alignment. V2V-Bench pairs diverse source videos with challenging editing tasks and evaluates two commercial models, Grok Imagine and Gemini Veo3, and one open-source model, Open Sora 2. Results show complementary model strengths: Grok performs better on editing fidelity, while Veo3 achieves stronger visual quality. On six V2V-specific dimensions, V2V-Bench reaches a Spearman correlation of 0.905 with human judgments.

</details>


### [35] [LongSpace: Exploring Long-Horizon Spatial Memory from Perception to Recall in Video](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05677)
*Shiqiang Lang,Jing Liu,Haoyang He,Peiwen Sun,Yuanteng Chen,Tao Liu,Lan Yang,Longteng Guo,Honggang Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces LongSpace-Bench, a benchmark for evaluating spatial memory in MLLMs, and presents LongSpace, a framework for enhancing long-video spatial reasoning.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To assess and enhance the ability of MLLMs to manage long-horizon tasks that require memory of spatial layouts and object states.

Method: LongSpace processes long videos in sequential chunks, integrates 3D structural cues into the decoder, and develops a memory architecture for guided retrieval of information.

Result: LongSpace demonstrates improved performance in spatial understanding across various benchmarks, evidencing the significance of spatial memory.

Conclusion: The study highlights the importance of explicit spatial memory for effective long-horizon video reasoning in MLLMs.

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) have advanced image and video understanding and can increasingly handle longer visual inputs. Long-horizon tasks such as autonomous driving and robotic navigation require more than recognizing the current view, as models must remember and retrieve previously observed spatial layouts, routes, viewpoint changes, and object states. To evaluate this capability, we introduce LongSpace-Bench, a room-tour video benchmark for long-horizon spatial memory, covering scene perception, spatial relations, and spatial memory. In this work, we further propose LongSpace, a memory framework for long-video spatial reasoning. LongSpace models long videos as sequential chunks, incorporates 3D structural cues into early decoder layers, and constructs layer-aware memory for question-guided retrieval. Experiments on multiple spatial reasoning benchmarks show that LongSpace improves long-video spatial understanding, further demonstrating explicit spatial memory as a key capability for long-horizon video MLLMs.

</details>


### [36] [T-SAR-JEPA: Self-Supervised Temporal Anomaly Detection in SAR Amplitude Stacks via Latent Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05700)
*Kerod Woldesenbet,Abem Woldesenbet*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: T-SAR-JEPA is a self-supervised framework for detecting temporal anomalies in SAR amplitude stacks, achieving significant performance improvement over existing methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance temporal anomaly detection in SAR data, addressing limitations of current techniques.

Method: Utilizes a ViT-Base/16 encoder for domain adaptation and a temporal transformer for forecasting future latent states, employing local masked reconstruction and gradient feature prediction.

Result: Achieves ROC-AUC of 77.0% on the DFC 2026 dataset, significantly surpassing traditional baselines like RX and LSTM, with high spatial coherence.

Conclusion: T-SAR-JEPA demonstrates effective anomaly detection through structured approach, leveraging a combination of modern self-supervised learning techniques.

Abstract: We present T-SAR-JEPA, a self-supervised framework for temporal anomaly detection in SAR amplitude stacks via latent prediction. A ViT-Base/16 encoder from SAR-JEPA is domain-adapted on 39,300 Capella patches using local masked reconstruction with gradient feature prediction. A temporal transformer with sinusoidal time encoding forecasts future latent states from K=7 acquisitions, with progressive unfreezing substantially reducing validation loss. The model operates on amplitude alone; InSAR coherence serves exclusively as independent pseudo-ground-truth. On the DFC 2026 dataset (300 time-series, three AOIs), T-SAR-JEPA achieves ROC-AUC of 77.0% on the Hawaii eruption window, outperforming RX, PaDiM, Linear AR, and LSTM baselines (~50%). Spatial coherence of 99.9% (p < 0.001, permutation test) confirms structured detections. Code: https://github.com/TerraLatent/t-sar-jepa

</details>


### [37] [Parallel Jacobi Decoding for Fast Autoregressive Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05703)
*Boya Liao,Ying Li,Siyong Jian,Huan Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: Parallel Jacobi Decoding (PJD) enhances the efficiency of autoregressive image generation models by enabling spatially parallel refinement, resulting in significant acceleration without sacrificing image quality.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the slow inference speed of autoregressive models due to sequential next-token prediction and the diminishing returns of Jacobi-style decoding.

Method: PJD employs a training-free approach that expands draft tokens in the two-dimensional spatial domain and modifies the attention mask to reduce error propagation and enhance convergence stability.

Result: PJD achieves a 4.8x-6.4x acceleration in generation speed across multiple autoregressive models while sustaining competitive image quality.

Conclusion: The proposed PJD technique significantly improves the efficiency of autoregressive image generation, leveraging local spatial correlations in images.

Abstract: Autoregressive (AR) models have demonstrated remarkable performance in generating high-fidelity images. However, their inherently sequential next-token prediction leads to significantly slower inference. Recent studies have introduced Jacobi-style decoding to accelerate autoregressive image generation. Extending the draft sequence initially improves efficiency, yet the acceleration quickly saturates as error propagation in the one-dimensional sequence hinders convergence. Observing that images exhibit strong local spatial correlations, we propose Parallel Jacobi Decoding (PJD), a training-free decoding approach that expands draft tokens in the two-dimensional spatial domain to enable efficient spatially parallel refinement. PJD adjusts the attention mask to mitigate error accumulation and improve convergence stability. Extensive experiments on diverse datasets show that PJD achieves 4.8x-6.4x acceleration across multiple autoregressive image generation models while maintaining competitive generation quality.

</details>


### [38] [Real-Time Threat Detection from Surveillance Cameras using Machine Learning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05708)
*Gajendra Mandal,J. P. Patra,Priyansh Mahant*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces a real-time object detection surveillance system aimed at enhancing public safety in urban areas by efficiently identifying weapons like guns and knives, as well as blunt objects, utilizing a custom dataset and YOLOv8 model.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation for this work is to improve public safety by addressing the inefficiencies and limitations of traditional manual surveillance systems, particularly in detecting violent objects in densely populated areas.

Method: The method involves developing a surveillance framework based on real-time object detection using a YOLOv8 model. It incorporates a custom dataset of 336 images of blunt objects and a public dataset of 7,623 images of weapons to form a comprehensive training set.

Result: Experimental results demonstrate that the training of the YOLOv8 model led to enhancements in recall and average precision specifically for the blunt object category, showing effectiveness without overfitting.

Conclusion: The framework achieves a satisfactory trade-off between accuracy and operational efficiency, making it viable for practical applications in various public domains.

Abstract: Ensuring public safety in densely populated urban environments remains a critical challenge, necessitating the deployment of intelligent and automated video surveillance systems. Traditional surveillance approaches rely heavily on manual monitoring, which is inefficient and susceptible to human fatigue, delayed response, and observational errors. To overcome these limitations, this work presents a real-time object detection-based surveillance framework. The proposed system focuses on detecting guns, knives, and region-specific blunt objects commonly involved in violent activities in Indian surveillance scenarios. A key contribution of this work is the use of a custom-created dataset collected using a mobile camera, consisting of 336 labeled images of blunt objects such as iron rods, wooden sticks, and plastic rods. This dataset is combined with a publicly available dataset of 7,623 images of guns and knives, forming a consolidated dataset of 7,959 images across three classes: gun, knife, and blunt object. The combined dataset is used to train a YOLOv8-based object detection model for real-time performance. Experimental evaluation shows that increasing the training duration significantly improves recall and average precision for the blunt object class without signs of overfitting. Overall, the proposed framework achieves an effective balance between accuracy and efficiency, making it suitable for deployment in real-world surveillance environments such as campuses, public spaces, and transportation areas.

</details>


### [39] [ViCuR: Visual Cues as Recoverable Privilege for Multimodal On-Policy Distillation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05718)
*Kanghui Tian,Siyuan Liu,Ziang Yan,Sheng Xia,Shuai Dong,Yi Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: ViCuR introduces visually grounded privileged-teacher distillation, enhancing multimodal reasoning by using visual cues instead of answer-side privilege, resulting in improved model performance across various benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the issue of train-test mismatch in multimodal reasoning caused by answer-side privileged supervision, which leads to shortcut imitation rather than foundation in visual evidence.

Method: ViCuR utilizes visual cues from the same input available during inference, incorporating a lightweight cue recovery module for effective visual evidence aggregation without altering inference processes.

Result: ViCuR outperforms traditional answer-based on-policy self-distillation by +1.19 and +1.24 in average performance across seven benchmarks and shows improvements over stronger-teacher OPD, exceeding baselines by +0.64 and +1.08, with consistent gains in out-of-domain scenarios at the 8B scale.

Conclusion: The research highlights the significance of teacher privilege design in multimodal on-policy distillation, asserting that it is as crucial as the teacher's strength for improving model reasoning.

Abstract: On-policy distillation (OPD) improves reasoning by training a student on trajectories sampled from its own policy under supervision from a teacher. In multimodal reasoning, a common extension is to use a privileged teacher that observes training-time-only signals such as reference answers or rationales. However, such answer-side privilege creates a train-test mismatch: the teacher's supervision may depend on signals unavailable to the student, encouraging shortcut imitation rather than visually grounded reasoning. We propose ViCuR, a visually grounded privileged-teacher distillation framework that replaces answer-side privilege with visual cues (query-related evidence in the input). Because these cues are derived from the same visual input available at inference, their evidence is recoverable by the student. To support this, ViCuR introduces a lightweight cue recovery module that uses dedicated sink-token cross-attention during prefill to aggregate task-relevant visual evidence into an internal representation, without changing the inference interface or requiring auxiliary cue-generation losses. Across seven benchmarks with Qwen3-VL-2B and 8B students, ViCuR consistently improves over answer-based on-policy self-distillation by +1.19 and +1.24 on overall average performance. It also extends naturally to stronger-teacher OPD, surpassing OPD baselines by +0.64 and +1.08, with consistent out-of-domain gains at the 8B scale. These results show that, in multimodal on-policy distillation, the design of teacher privilege is as important as teacher strength.

</details>


### [40] [TextWand: A Unified Framework for Scene Text Editing](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05730)
*Shuyu Wang,Zhile Guan,Hongxiu Chen,Yule Duan,Weiqi Li,Xin Shan,Ronggang Wang,Jian Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: TextWand is a framework that integrates scene text removal, generation, and replacement. It employs novel encoding and suppression strategies for high-fidelity editing and introduces a benchmark for evaluation.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation behind TextWand is to provide a unified solution for complex scene text editing tasks that have previously been handled by separate models, by ensuring text appearance control and background integrity.

Method: TextWand employs Overlay-Reference Positional Encoding (ORPE) for pixel-level layout fidelity and Region-Adaptive Suppression (RAS) for effective text erasure.

Result: TextWand significantly outperforms existing models in terms of text content accuracy, layout and style consistency, and image quality across various text editing tasks.

Conclusion: The results indicate that TextWand is an effective and superior framework for scene text editing, addressing the limitations of previous models while establishing a new benchmark for the field.

Abstract: We propose TextWand, a general-purpose framework that unifies scene text removal, generation, and replacement into a single model. By decomposing complex editing tasks into the atomic primitives of rendering and erasure, TextWand achieves precise control over both text appearance and background integrity. Specifically, we introduce a novel design, Overlay-Reference Positional Encoding (ORPE), to enforce pixel-level layout fidelity and exemplar-driven style control, alongside a new strategy, Region-Adaptive Suppression (RAS), to ensure clean text erasure. To address the absence of a comprehensive benchmark for general-purpose scene text editing among existing single-task datasets, we construct TextWand-Bench. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TextWand outperforms existing leading open-source and closed-source models by delivering superior text content accuracy, layout and style consistency, and overall image quality across scene text removal, generation and replacement tasks.

</details>


### [41] [VTI-CoT: Visual-Textual Interleaved Chain of Thought for Video Reasoning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05736)
*Shufan Zhang,Ziyue Lin,Bairun Wang,Lei Jin,Xuanding Ding,Xinzhu Ma,Kunlin Yang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: VTI-CoT enhances video reasoning by integrating visual and textual information via an automated annotation pipeline, improving efficiency and performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve reasoning accuracy in video event interpretation by combining visual data with textual logic, addressing the limitations of current CoT-based methods that rely solely on text.

Method: VTI-CoT employs a Visual-Textual Interleaved framework that pairs reasoning steps with visual frames and uses OCR-based compression for scalability in training with long-form videos.

Result: VTI-CoT outperforms existing models of similar parameter size and increases training efficiency, thanks to its innovative integration of multimodal data.

Conclusion: The proposed VTI-CoT framework sets a new standard in video reasoning by providing a combined approach to visual and textual analysis, leading to enhanced results.

Abstract: Video reasoning aims to understand complex temporal events and causal relationships within videos. Recently, Chain-of-Thought (CoT) has been introduced to this field to enhance reasoning accuracy. However, existing CoT-based video reasoning methods primarily rely on text-only information for logical deduction, overlooking critical visual information during the inference process. Inspired by the human cognitive mechanism of reviewing visual segments during inference, we propose VTI-CoT, a Visual-Textual Interleaved CoT framework. VTI-CoT integrates textual reasoning steps with corresponding visual frames. Given the scarcity of visual-textual interleaved CoT in existing datasets, we develop an automated annotation pipeline to construct high-quality multimodal CoT data. Further, reasoning over long-form videos entails increasingly long CoT token sequences, which severely hinders training convergence and efficiency. To address this, we employ Optical Character Recognition (OCR)-based compression techniques to compress CoT supervision signals into a single canvas. Experimental results demonstrate that VTI-CoT achieves state-of-the-art performance among models of the same parameter scale while significantly improving training efficiency.

</details>


### [42] [Let It Be Simple: One-Step Action Generation for Vision-Language-Action Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05737)
*Yitong Chen,Shiduo Zhang,Jingjing Gong,Xipeng Qiu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper examines one-step action generation in diffusion-based vision-language-action models, arguing that it can be effectively achieved without complex methods used in image synthesis by conditioning on rich observations and employing a high-noise training bias.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To challenge the assumption that one-step action generation in VLA models requires sophisticated techniques similar to those in image generation.

Method: The study utilizes standard velocity prediction while shifting the training distribution towards high-noise states, testing this approach on MNIST and various robot-policy tasks without additional models or objectives.

Result: One-step policies trained under the high-noise bias match or exceed the performance of ten-step decoding in some scenarios, highlighting the effectiveness of this simpler approach.

Conclusion: Strong one-step VLA action generation can be effectively achieved within the framework of standard diffusion training, without needing to incorporate complex few-step diffusion strategies.

Abstract: Diffusion-based vision-language-action (VLA) models often inherit the image-generation view: actions are generated by iterative denoising. We argue that VLA action generation has a different condition-target structure: the policy is conditioned on rich observations, language, and state, but predicts only a compact, low-dimensional action chunk. Under this asymmetry, strong one-step action generation should not necessarily require the advanced one-step methods developed for image synthesis. We keep standard velocity prediction and add no teacher model, distillation stage, or auxiliary objective; in our main recipe, we simply bias the training time distribution toward high-noise states. We first isolate the effect in a controlled MNIST grid-to-sequence task, then test it with extensive robot-policy experiments. Across standard LIBERO, LIBERO-Plus, and LIBERO-Pro, one-step policies trained with high-noise biased schedules generally match ten-step decoding under the same recipe, and on standard LIBERO can exceed ten-step policies trained with a uniform time distribution. A real-robot bimanual YAM RSS evaluation gives a small-sample cross-architecture check of the same sampler trend. On a 1.4B VLM model with a 30M action head, one-step decoding reaches 95.6\% on LIBERO-Long. These results show that strong one-step VLA action generation can emerge from standard diffusion training, without importing the full few-step diffusion machinery developed for image generation.

</details>


### [43] [Cosine Misleads: Auxiliary Losses Reshape Vision Language Models, Not Their Latents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05753)
*XiuYu Zhang,Junfeng Fang,Zhenkai Liang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This study challenges the effectiveness of supervised latent tokens in latent visual reasoning for vision-language models, revealing a negative correlation between cosine alignment and accuracy, and introducing diagnostics that suggest these latents are often bypassed in decoding answers.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To investigate the effectiveness of supervised latent tokens in vision-language models and their assumed role in improving accuracy through alignment with visual targets.

Method: The study employed a matrix of five LVR variants to analyze the correlation between cosine alignment and accuracy, and introduced PRISM diagnostics to evaluate the decodability of answers and the functionality of latent variables.

Result: Found a negative correlation (r=-0.94) between cosine alignment and model accuracy, with evidence that supervised latents are often bypassed and have minimal impact on accuracy when corrupted.

Conclusion: The auxiliary objective in LVR reshapes the language model's performance through shared parameters rather than enhancing the latent's utility, aligning with the Information Bottleneck theory.

Abstract: Latent visual reasoning (LVR) inserts supervised latent tokens between perception and answer generation in vision-language models (VLMs). The field uses alignment between these latents and their visual targets, i.e., cosine similarity or mean squared error (MSE), as both the training loss and the quality metric, assuming that better alignment yields a better answer. We test this with a designed matrix of five LVR variants and find the assumption inverted: cosine alignment is negatively correlated with accuracy across all five (r=-0.94). To explain this, we introduce PRISM, a pair of inference-time diagnostics: a linear probe that asks where the answer is decodable, and a corruption test that asks whether the latent is load-bearing. The supervised latents are largely bypassed. Corrupting them shifts accuracy by at most four points. The answer is decodable downstream of the latent but not at it, and the size of this decodability gap predicts how much each variant relies on its latent under perturbation. Consistent with an Information Bottleneck reading of the loss, the auxiliary objective reshapes the language model via shared parameters rather than via the latent variable it nominally optimizes.

</details>


### [44] [DRIFT: A Residual Flow Adapter for Decoding Continuous Outputs in Vision-Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05758)
*Zhuoming Liu,Jinhong Lin,Kwan Man Cheng,Lin Zhang,Shayok Bagchi,Yin Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: DRIFT is a framework designed to enhance vision-language models for continuous output tasks by combining coarse prediction with generative refinement.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve the adaptation of pretrained vision-language models to tasks requiring continuous outputs, which traditional autoregressive decoding struggles with.

Method: DRIFT employs a base predictor for coarse estimation and a generative refinement module based on flow matching to iteratively enhance output predictions.

Result: DRIFT demonstrates superior performance across various tasks including visual grounding and robotic control when compared to several regression and generative solutions.

Conclusion: The proposed framework simplifies optimization challenges in continuous output tasks and consistently outperforms existing methods.

Abstract: Many modern vision-language models (VLMs) build on autoregressive decoding of discrete tokens. While text-based output interfaces enable scalable pretraining and strong zero-shot generalization across diverse tasks, they are poorly suited for problems that require precise continuous outputs, such as localizing temporal boundaries of events or generating robotic control actions. To address this challenge, we propose DRIFT, a general framework for adapting pretrained VLMs to continuous decoding tasks. DRIFT combines a base predictor, which provides a coarse estimate of the target output, with a generative refinement module based on flow matching that iteratively improves the prediction. This residual formulation transforms the generative modeling problem from learning a global output distribution to modeling a localized residual distribution around a strong prior, substantially simplifying optimization. We evaluate DRIFT on both perception and planning tasks, including visual grounding and robotic control. Across multiple tasks and architectures spanning MLLMs, VLAs, and WAMs, DRIFT consistently outperforms a strong set of regression- and generative-based solutions.

</details>


### [45] [Physics-Guided Deep Unfolding for Blind Cross-Sensor Spectral Super-Resolution via Learning the Spectral Transformation Function](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05759)
*Zhaolin Li,Jinsong Chen,Shanxin Guo,Tuo Zhang,Xinglong Zhang,Pan Chen*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents PGU-Net, a deep learning model for recovering hyperspectral images from multispectral images in cross-sensor scenarios, addressing the challenge of unknown spectral response functions.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing spectral super-resolution methods are limited by their assumptions of known spectral response functions and single-sensor deployments, needing better solutions for real-world cross-sensor applications.

Method: PGU-Net involves a deep unfolding network that alternates between estimating hyperspectral images and a learnable spectral transformation function, combining proximal networks with closed-form solvers for physical interpretability.

Result: Experiments show that PGU-Net accurately recovers spectral transformation functions and enhances reconstruction quality, surpassing traditional SSR techniques on benchmark datasets and performing well in real UAV scenarios.

Conclusion: PGU-Net effectively operates under blind conditions, demonstrating robustness and accuracy in estimating spectral transformations, indicating potential for applications in land-cover differentiation.

Abstract: Hyperspectral imaging provides rich spectral information for quantitative remote sensing, yet hyperspectral sensors remain costly and thus unavailable in many UAV deployments. Spectral super-resolution (SSR) seeks to reconstruct hyperspectral images (HSIs) from multispectral images (MSIs). Most existing SSR methods assume a fixed and known spectral response function (SRF) and are therefore limited to single-sensor settings. In practical cross-sensor scenarios, the spectral degradation from HSI to MSI is unknown and varies with sensor characteristics and scene content, which renders HSI reconstruction ill-posed. This paper proposes a physics-guided deep unfolding network, termed PGU-Net, to address blind cross-sensor SSR by jointly estimating the HSI and a learnable spectral transformation function (STF). PGU-Net unrolls an alternating optimization procedure into an end-to-end trainable architecture with stages, where each stage sequentially updates the HSI and the STF. Both modules combine learnable proximal networks with differentiable closed-form solvers, enabling physical interpretability while retaining strong representation capacity. Experiments on benchmark datasets (CAVE and NTIRE 2022) with multiple SRFs demonstrate accurate recovery of the STF (degradation operator) and improved reconstruction performance over state-of-the-art SSR methods. Furthermore, evaluations on a real UAV cross-sensor dataset (Headwall Nano HSI and DJI P4 Multispectral MSI) verify the effectiveness and robustness of PGU-Net under truly blind conditions, and suggest that the estimated STF may exhibit land-cover-related differences.

</details>


### [46] [ExpSpeech-Net: Multimodal Fusion of Expression and Speech for Deepfake Detection](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05760)
*Ruchika Sharma,Rudresh Dwivedi*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents ExpSpeech-Net, a lightweight model for deepfake detection using SqueezeNet and RNN, achieving superior performance with high accuracy and precision.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the challenges posed by deepfake videos and limitations of existing detection methods, especially their complexity and resource demands.

Method: The study employs a hybrid approach integrating SqueezeNet and RNN, using advanced feature extraction techniques (ISLBT for images and MPNCC for audio signals) and a smart feature-selection strategy with SASMA.

Result: The proposed model achieved an accuracy of 94.5%, precision of 99.3%, and an F-measure of 96.8%, surpassing traditional detection methods.

Conclusion: The integration of multiple modalities and effective feature selection facilitates practical, real-time deepfake detection for everyday applications.

Abstract: Deepfake videos are increasingly challenging the credibility of online content. Many existing detection methodology relies on complex, resource-intensive models, which limit their practical use. The study introduces the ExpSpeech-Net deepfake detection (SqN-R-DFD) model, which utilizes SqueezeNet and RNN (Recurrent Neural Network) as its backbone, providing a lightweight and efficient deepfake detection framework that simultaneously analyzes facial expressions and speech patterns. The approach incorporates advanced feature extraction, such as ISLBT-based features for image and MPNCC for signals, along with a smart feature-selection strategy using SASMA (Sandpiper-Assisted Slime Mould Algorithm), ensuring optimal and balanced input to the detection models. By combining SqueezeNet and an RNN, subtle inconsistencies in deepfake videos are captured effectively. The framework achieves 94.5% accuracy, precision of 99.3%, and F-measure of 96.8%, outperforming conventional methods. This demonstrates that integrating multiple modalities with intelligent preprocessing and feature selection enables practical, real-time deepfake detection suitable for everyday applications.

</details>


### [47] [Imagine Before You Predict: Interleaved Latent Visual Reasoning for Video Event Prediction](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05769)
*Tianxiang Jiang,Linquan Wu,Sheng Xia,Songze Li,Ziang Yan,Haoyu Yang,Yu Qiao,Yi Wang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces Future-L1, a new framework for video event prediction that integrates visual reasoning with language processing to enhance predictive accuracy while preserving visual semantics.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Existing models often lose detailed visual information by verbalizing future reasoning, leading to unreliable predictions. Future-L1 aims to maintain intermediate visual cues for better accuracy in video event prediction.

Method: Future-L1 employs a dual approach, interleaving language tokens with latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding, and is trained on a carefully constructed dataset (Future-L1-50K) optimized with a latent-aware RL objective (LA-DAPO) focusing on outcome contrast and temporal diversity.

Result: Future-L1 achieves state-of-the-art performance, significantly improving existing benchmarks: it raises Qwen3-VL-8B's score on FutureBench from 61.0 to 85.4 and surpasses previous best results on TwiFF-Bench from 2.44 to 3.04.

Conclusion: The findings indicate that preserving intermediate visual semantics during reasoning enhances future-oriented video reasoning, leading to more reliable predictions.

Abstract: Video event prediction (VEP) requires models to infer unobserved future states from partial video evidence. Existing video MLLMs usually verbalize intermediate future reasoning in text space: once visual evidence is verbalized, fine-grained motion, geometry, and interaction cues can be lost, leading to plausible but visually ungrounded hallucinations. We introduce Future-L1, an interleaved latent visual reasoning framework that lets an MLLM alternate between language tokens and continuous latent visual spans during autoregressive decoding. To train this capability, we construct Future-L1-50K by selecting examples where future visual hints help prediction and align latent states to future-frame embeddings, then further optimize sampled latent trajectories with LA-DAPO, a latent-aware RL objective with outcome-contrastive and temporal-diversity rewards. Future-L1 achieves new state-of-the-art results on both benchmarks: on FutureBench, it improves Qwen3-VL-8B from 61.0 to 85.4 and exceeds the previous best Video-CoE by 10.4 points; on TwiFF-Bench, it improves the average score from 2.44 to 3.04. These results suggest that future-oriented video reasoning benefits from preserving intermediate visual semantics in latent space rather than translating every reasoning step into text.

</details>


### [48] [LiAuto-GeoX: Efficient Grounded Driving Transformer](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05774)
*Jiawei Lian,Haoyi Sun,Yang Wu,Lifu Mu,Siyuan Wang,Le Hui,Ning Mao,Tao Wei,Pan Zhou,Kun Zhan,Jian Yang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: LiAuto-GeoX is a new efficient grounded driving transformer for real-time dense 3D reconstruction in autonomous driving, achieving high spatial understanding with less computational demand.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The paper addresses the challenges of large-scale visual geometry models in autonomous driving, which require high computational resources and fail to deliver the necessary geometric fidelity and efficiency in dynamic environments.

Method: LiAuto-GeoX learns a driving geometry model from extensive surround-view data, employing sparse LiDAR data for robust geometric grounding. It uses a compact 155M-parameter onboard model optimized through a geometry-preserving distillation framework, which retains important geometric details and ensures spatial consistency.

Result: The model achieves 220 FPS on the KITTI benchmark with high-fidelity dense reconstruction and demonstrates strong performance in various autonomous driving tasks, including trajectory and occupancy predictions.

Conclusion: LiAuto-GeoX illustrates that efficient dense 3D reconstruction can become a scalable, foundational representation for advanced autonomous driving systems.

Abstract: Dense 3D reconstruction has demonstrated immense potential for spatial understanding, yet its viability as a real-time, onboard representation for autonomous driving remains an open challenge. Existing large-scale visual geometry models typically require substantial computational resources and lack the long-range geometric fidelity, surround-view consistency, and real-time efficiency demanded by dynamic driving environments. To bridge this gap, we present \textbf{LiAuto-GeoX}, an efficient grounded driving transformer designed for deployable, ego-centric 3D scene understanding. Our approach begins by learning a high-capacity driving geometry model from large-scale surround-view data, utilizing sparse LiDAR priors to provide robust geometric grounding in distant, ambiguous, or structure-sparse regions. We then instantiate this capability into a highly compact 155M-parameter onboard model through a novel geometry-preserving distillation framework. This framework employs mask-guided depth-aware distillation to retain fine-grained metric structures by emphasizing geometrically informative regions, and relative-pose relational distillation to enforce cross-view spatial consistency through pose-induced geometric relations. Extensive evaluations reveal that \textbf{LiAuto-GeoX} runs at 220 FPS on KITTI while maintaining high-fidelity dense reconstruction, enabling real-time deployment. The learned geometry transfers seamlessly to downstream autonomy tasks, achieving 90.6 PDMS in trajectory prediction, 24.63 mIoU in occupancy prediction, and 47.67 IoU in future-frame prediction. These all demonstrate that efficient dense 3D reconstruction can transcend its traditional role as a perception target to serve as a scalable, foundational geometric representation for next-generation autonomous driving.

</details>


### [49] [Beyond Absolute Scores: Relative Edit-induced Difference for Generalizable Image Aesthetic Assessment](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05778)
*Qifei Jia,Xintong Yao,Minghao Li,Yajie Chai,Qiming Lu,Baoyue Shen,Yasen Zhang,Runyu Shi,Ying Huang,Yue Zhang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces RED-Aes, a framework for Image Aesthetic Assessment that learns from relative aesthetic differences instead of absolute scores, addressing the limitations of traditional methods.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the shortcomings of traditional IAA methods that rely on absolute scores, which fail to capture the dynamic nature of human aesthetic perception.

Method: The RED-Aes framework uses controllable image editing models to simulate human aesthetic reasoning and learns visual factors driving aesthetic changes. It is supported by the RED-20k dataset and employs a three-stage training strategy with relative ranking consistency reward.

Result: RED-Aes achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple benchmarks and demonstrates enhanced generalization across diverse scenarios.

Conclusion: The proposed framework improves aesthetic assessment by emphasizing relative differences, allowing for better alignment with human aesthetic reasoning.

Abstract: Traditional Image Aesthetic Assessment (IAA) methods mainly rely on regressing absolute Mean Opinion Scores (MOS). However, such a paradigm overlooks the inherently dynamic nature of human aesthetic perception, which relies on subconscious comparison against implicit visual references. Consequently, the lack of causal reasoning regarding aesthetic differences prevents models from learning generalizable aesthetic principles, thus limiting their generalization across diverse scenarios. In this work, we rethink the IAA task and propose Relative Edit-induced Difference Aesthetic learning (RED-Aes), a novel framework that leverages controllable image editing models to simulate the human aesthetic reasoning process. Instead of fitting absolute score distributions, RED-Aes explicitly learns the visual factors that drive aesthetic changes. To support this paradigm, we construct the RED-20k dataset, which comprises editing-based image pairs, quantitative aesthetic differences, and Chain-of-Thought (CoT) reasoning. Furthermore, we introduce a three-stage training strategy guided by a relative ranking consistency reward, optimizing the model solely via relative supervision. Extensive experiments demonstrate that RED-Aes achieves state-of-the-art performance on multiple public benchmarks, exhibiting superior generalization capabilities.

</details>


### [50] [Next-Generation Parallel Decoder for LPDR: Architectural Optimization and Class-Balanced GAN-Augmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05785)
*Shawaiz Obaid,Nida Chandio,Neha Jamil,Muhammad Khuram Shahzad*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents improvements in license plate detection and recognition through novel techniques addressing data imbalance and spatial mismatches, resulting in enhanced recognition rates and real-time performance.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To overcome performance limitations in the YOLOV5-PDLPR model due to spatial character mismatches and training set data imbalance.

Method: Introduction of Cross-Spatial Hybrid Attention (CSHA) and Class-Balanced Synthetic Augmentation (CBSA), along with evaluation on four benchmarks using 75,000 synthetic samples.

Result: Improved recognition rate for minority provincial license plates from 78.2% to 91.5% while achieving a processing rate of 152 FPS.

Conclusion: Combining spatially-aware parallel decoding with class-balanced augmentation significantly enhances the efficiency of high-speed license plate recognition systems.

Abstract: Real-Time License Plate Detection and Recognition (LPDR) forms the backbone of modern smart cities. Although the YOLOV5-PDLPR model substantially improved system efficiency through a parallel decoder approach, its performance is still affected by spatial character mismatches and data imbalance within the training set. This paper addresses these limitations by introducing Cross-Spatial Hybrid Attention (CSHA) and Class-Balanced Synthetic Augmentation (CBSA). An extensive study involving 75,000 synthetic samples is conducted and evaluated on four benchmarks: CCPD, CLPD, PKU, and an application-specific dataset. Experimental results demonstrate a substantial improvement in the recognition rate of minority provincial license plates from 78.2% to 91.5% while maintaining real-time processing performance of 152 FPS. The results indicate that spatially-aware parallel decoding combined with class-balanced augmentation provides an effective solution for high-speed license plate recognition systems.

</details>


### [51] [Emotion-Aware Image Generation from Korean Diary Text via LLM-based Prompt Translation and LoRA Fine-Tuning](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05816)
*Jihun Cho,Soo-Yeon Jeong,Sun-Young Ihm*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents an emotion-aware text-to-image pipeline that generates children's drawing style images from Korean diary entries, addressing limitations in sentiment capture by traditional T2I models.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To improve the generation of images that reflect sentiments in text, particularly from diary entries, which typical T2I models struggle with due to their focus on visual objects rather than emotional context.

Method: A combined approach utilizing Qwen3-8B for sentiment recognition from diaries and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium fine-tuned with LoRA for generating images based on emotion-trigger words.

Result: Experimentation showed the impact of emotion-trigger words on the images generated, highlighting the necessity for better evaluation metrics.

Conclusion: The study underscores the limitations of using CLIP Score for assessing emotion-aware image generation and suggests enhancements to understand and translate sentiment in visual outputs.

Abstract: T2I models cannot effectively capture sentiment from various types of text, including diaries, as they primarily focus on visual object-related patterns rather than contextual emotional understanding. This paper proposes an emotion-aware text-to-image pipeline that generates children's hand drawing style images from short Korean diary entries. The proposed pipeline employs Qwen3-8B for recognising implicit sentiment from short diaries, and Stable Diffusion 3.5 Medium fine-tuned with LoRA on children's drawing images with emotion-based trigger words for image generation. Additionally, this paper presents experiments examining the effect of emotion trigger words on generated images and discusses the limitations of CLIP Score as an evaluation metric for emotion-aware image generation.

</details>


### [52] [Gender Artifacts from Art History to Text-to-Image Generation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05829)
*Piera Riccio,Miriam Doh,Benedikt Höltgen,Noa Garcia,Nanne van Noord*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper introduces the StyleGender dataset, exploring the relationship between gender representation and artistic styles in images, including historical and generated content.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To analyze the interplay between gender representation and artistic styles, addressing a gap in AI that treats style merely as a superficial property rather than a complex socio-historical construct.

Method: The study utilizes a new dataset of 74k images across 19 styles, incorporating historical and generated art, along with two Set Gender Artifact metrics to assess gender representation.

Result: Findings indicate that gender representation influences visual features in styles, style keywords affect T2I generation, and generative models exaggerate gender artifacts compared to historical sources.

Conclusion: The work highlights the significance of integrating socio-historical context into AI methodologies for better understanding artistic styles and gender representation.

Abstract: Artistic styles are rooted in specific socio-historical contexts that encode social hierarchies, including distinct constructions of gender. Yet in AI research, style has long been treated as a surface-level visual property: a filter of color, brushstroke, and texture applied to otherwise content-neutral scenes. We introduce the first dataset to investigate the interplay between gender representation and style in both historical and generated images. StyleGender comprises 74k images spanning 19 artistic styles, comprising art historical images with style and gender annotations, T2I-generated images under controlled style and gender prompts, and a semantically aligned set enabling direct art history-to-generation comparison. By proposing two Set Gender Artifact (SGA) metrics (PixelSGA and MaskSGA), capturing gender signals at the pixel level and in compositional structure, we show that (1) gender representation shapes visual features across artistic styles, (2) style keywords carry these patterns into T2I generation, and (3) generative models tend to amplify gender artifacts beyond what is observed in historical sources.

</details>


### [53] [Learning Geometric Representations from Videos for Spatial Intelligent Multimodal Large Language Models](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05833)
*Haibo Wang,Lifu Huang*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: GeoVR is a novel framework that enhances MLLMs' 3D awareness by using 2D video sequences to learn geometric representations, outperforming existing spatial reasoning benchmarks.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the lack of geometric and spatial consistency in MLLMs due to their intrinsic limitation in 3D awareness and the challenge of obtaining large-scale 3D data.

Method: GeoVR reconfigures the semantic latent space of MLLMs by distilling knowledge from pre-trained 3D models through a multi-objective learning strategy targeting various geometric aspects, including camera poses, depth maps, scale factors, and multi-scale 3D features.

Result: Extensive experiments indicate that GeoVR achieves state-of-the-art results in spatial reasoning tasks, demonstrating its effectiveness in enhancing 3D awareness in MLLMs.

Conclusion: GeoVR establishes a new paradigm for integrating spatial intelligence into foundation models, significantly improving their 3D representation capabilities.

Abstract: Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) excel at 2D semantic understanding but lack intrinsic 3D awareness, resulting in representations that fail to maintain geometric and spatial consistency across video frames. Given the scarcity of large-scale 3D data, we present GeoVR, a novel framework that learns geometric representations using purely 2D video sequences. This approach effectively restructures the semantic latent space within MLLMs to unlock spatial intelligence. Rather than employing superficial feature mixing, GeoVR reshapes the internal representations of the MLLM by distilling geometry knowledge from pre-trained 3D foundation models. This is accomplished through a multi-objective learning strategy driven by four complementary geometric targets: (1) estimating inter-frame camera poses to embed varying viewpoint dynamics, (2) regressing dense depth maps to anchor physical distances, (3) predicting a metric scale factor for real-world calibration, and (4) distilling multi-scale 3D features to align the intermediate feature space. Guided by these explicit physical and geometric constraints, the model's internal representations naturally develop strong 3D awareness. Extensive experiments on spatial reasoning benchmarks demonstrate that GeoVR achieves state-of-the-art performance, establishing a new paradigm for endowing foundation models with spatial intelligence.

</details>


### [54] [Geometry-Aware Dataset Condensation for Diffusion Model Training](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05883)
*Xiao Cui,Yulei Qin,Mo Zhu,Wengang Zhou,Hongsheng Li,Houqiang Li*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a novel approach to dataset condensation for diffusion model training by reformulating real subset selection as a geometry-aware distribution alignment problem, ensuring high fidelity and proper geometric structure.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: Current methods for dataset condensation are ineffective for diffusion model training due to their inability to generate high-quality synthetic data or effectively select real data subsets that maintain necessary distributional geometry.

Method: The proposed method uses one-sided partial optimal transport for geometry-aware distribution alignment, allowing for unmatched mass in low-density regions and employs a two-stage discrete optimization strategy for alignment.

Result: The method demonstrates superior fidelity and distributional coverage in training diffusion models through comprehensive experiments across various parameters.

Conclusion: This approach effectively preserves geometric structures and enhances dataset alignment, significantly benefiting the training of diffusion models.

Abstract: Dataset condensation aims to construct compact datasets from real data via synthesis or selection. However, existing approaches are ill-suited for diffusion model training: synthetic data generation often yields low-fidelity samples unsuitable for authentic modeling, while real subset selection typically fails to preserve the distributional geometry required by diffusion likelihood objectives. To address this, we propose to reformulate real subset selection as a geometry-aware distribution alignment problem. By incorporating one-sided partial optimal transport, our method selectively aligns a compact subset with the full data distribution while allowing unmatched mass in low-density regions, ensuring the preserved geometric structure necessary for effective diffusion model training. To further ensure distributional fidelity, we complement geometric alignment with lightweight feature-statistics and semantic consistency regularization. An efficient two-stage discrete optimization strategy is proposed to achieve this alignment objective. Extensive experiments across diffusion variants, subset sizes, image resolutions, and training rounds show that our method achieves superior fidelity and distributional coverage in diffusion model training. Codes are available at https://github.com/2018cx/GADC.

</details>


### [55] [Resonant Minds: Closed-Loop Social Avatars with Theory of Mind](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05896)
*Jianxu Shangguan,Jing Xu,Hang Ye,Xiaoxuan Ma,Yizhou Wang,Wentao Zhu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: The paper presents a dual-agent framework that integrates perception, social reasoning, and expression for creating lifelike digital humans capable of genuine social interaction.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To unify cognitive reasoning and multimodal generation for lifelike digital humans, addressing limitations in current models that treat dialogue and visual expression as separate tasks.

Method: A closed-loop dual-agent framework is proposed, combining perception analysis of partners' behaviors, social reasoning for inferring mental states, and expression generation for videos that depict interactive dynamics.

Result: The framework demonstrates competitive performance in dialogue quality and video generation against state-of-the-art approaches, particularly excelling in generating thoughtful dialogue under conditions of information asymmetry.

Conclusion: The results indicate that inferring mental states under uncertainty results in more meaningful interactions compared to unrestricted information access, underscoring the importance of integration in digital human technologies.

Abstract: Creating lifelike digital humans with genuine social intelligence requires unifying cognitive reasoning and multimodal generation within a coherent framework. Current approaches treat these as separate tasks: Large Language Models excel at dialogue but lack embodied expression, while diffusion-based talking head models achieve visual fidelity but ignore social cognition. To bridge this gap, we propose a closed-loop dual-agent framework integrating perception, social reasoning, and expression into a continuous interaction cycle. The perception module analyzes partners' multimodal behaviors from video, while the social reasoning module infers hidden mental states through Theory of Mind and selects responses via an ensemble mechanism. The expression module then generates emotion-controllable dual-agent videos synthesizing both speaker speech and expression alongside listener reactive behaviors, capturing bidirectional dynamics absent in prior work. We construct a hierarchical Persona-Scenario dataset with psychologically grounded personas and private social goals to support evaluation under information asymmetry. Experiments on this dataset demonstrate competitive or superior performance on both dialogue quality and video generation metrics. Notably, our method surpasses even the full-information Script mode on key dialogue quality dimensions, suggesting that explicit mental state inference under uncertainty can elicit more thoughtful dialogue than unrestricted information access.

</details>


### [56] [CamFlow+: Hybrid Motion Bases for 2D Camera Motion Estimation with Stabilization Applications](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05915)
*Haipeng Li,Zhen Liu,Zhanglei Yang,Hai Jiang,Tianhao Zhou,Zhengzhe Liu,Ping Tan,Bing Zeng,Shuaicheng Liu*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: CamFlow+ introduces a hybrid-basis framework for estimating 2D camera motion, addressing challenges in existing methods by integrating diverse motion representations for improved accuracy in dense-flow space.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To enhance the accuracy of 2D camera motion estimation where traditional homography-based methods falter due to limitations like camera translation and depth variation.

Method: CamFlow+ utilizes a combination of homography-derived, stochastic, and depth-translational bases to represent motion, along with a depth-aware smoothness term to manage parallax effects.

Result: CamFlow+ outperforms existing methods in both sparse and dense camera-motion estimation and improves stabilizing digital video footage, showing superior preference in user studies.

Conclusion: By relaxing assumptions of a single plane, CamFlow+ provides better performance in estimating camera motion and stabilizing video, highlighting its effectiveness in practical applications.

Abstract: Estimating 2D camera motion is fundamental to computer vision and computational photography. Existing homography-based methods work well for planar scenes or pure rotation, but struggle with camera translation, depth variation, and local parallax; local homography and mesh-based models improve flexibility but still rely on piecewise planar assumptions. We introduce CamFlow+, a hybrid-basis framework that represents 2D camera motion directly in dense-flow space. CamFlow+ combines homography-derived physical bases, stochastic bases sampled from homography flows, and depth-translational bases derived from depth and camera intrinsics, relaxing the single-plane constraint while preserving camera-motion regularity. A depth-aware smoothness term further regularizes translation-induced parallax in continuous-depth regions while preserving motion changes near depth boundaries. We evaluate CamFlow+ on GHOF-Cam, a camera-motion benchmark that masks out dynamic objects and ill-posed occlusion regions in an optical-flow benchmark to isolate camera-induced motion. Experiments show that CamFlow+ improves sparse and dense camera-motion estimation. In digital video stabilization, CamFlow+ also improves global and local stability, achieving the best top-1 preference rate in a blind user study. Code and datasets will be available on the project page: https://lhaippp.github.io/CamFlow+.

</details>


### [57] [Self-Learning Expression Deformations for Data-Efficient Gaussian Avatars](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05912)
*Jiahao Yang,Xiaohang Yang,Qing Wang,Yilan Dong,Gregory Slabaugh,Shanxin Yuan*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents the SAGE framework for animating expressive avatars using minimal input through self-learning Gaussian deformations.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The motivation is to address the challenges of modeling dynamic facial expressions with 3D Gaussian representations, especially concerning scalability and the extensive data requirements of existing methods.

Method: SAGE optimizes 2D Gaussian surfels and Signed Distance Fields to create compact Gaussian distributions, integrating self-supervised expression learning to replace lengthy training sequences with consistency constraints.

Result: Experiments show that SAGE achieves high-quality facial animation comparable to state-of-the-art techniques while drastically reducing the amount of required input data.

Conclusion: The results suggest that SAGE paves the way for efficient avatar creation using self-supervised learning of Gaussian deformations.

Abstract: Modeling dynamic facial expressions using 3D Gaussian representations remains challenging due to their unstructured nature. Conventional Gaussian avatar pipelines require extensive multiview and sequential expression data, limiting scalability and accessibility. In this work, we introduce Self-Adaptive Gaussian Expression (SAGE), a framework for self-learning expression-induced Gaussian deformations that enables high-fidelity, animatable avatars from minimal input data. Our method jointly optimizes 2D Gaussian surfels and a Signed Distance Field (SDF) to enforce compact, surface-aligned Gaussian distributions, while a self-supervised expression learning phase replaces long training sequences with geometric and appearance consistency constraints. This design allows flexible deployment across multiple reconstruction regimes: in the multiview setting, only a single frame (timestep) is required instead of thousands; in the monocular setting, only head rotations are needed without expression sequences; and in the one-shot setting, no pretraining or priors are necessary. Experiments demonstrate that our approach achieves reconstruction and animation quality comparable to state-of-the-art methods, while reducing data requirements by several orders of magnitude. Our results highlight the potential of self-supervised Gaussian deformation learning as a step toward accessible, data-efficient avatar creation.

</details>


### [58] [T-FunS3D: Task-Driven Hierarchical Open-Vocabulary 3D Functionality Segmentation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05975)
*Jingkun Feng,Reza Sabzevari*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: T-FunS3D is a method for open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation that enhances robotic perception by efficiently identifying functional object components using 3D point clouds and RGB-D images.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: To address the challenges in open-vocabulary 3D segmentation and improve performance in terms of accuracy, granularity, and speed for robotic applications.

Method: T-FunS3D uses 3D point clouds and RGB-D images to create an open-vocabulary scene graph, identifying relevant instances based on task descriptions through a vision-language model.

Result: Experiments show T-FunS3D achieves comparable performance to state-of-the-art methods in segmentation while being faster and requiring less memory.

Conclusion: T-FunS3D represents a significant advancement in task-driven 3D functionality segmentation, enhancing robotic capabilities in understanding and interacting with complex indoor environments.

Abstract: Open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation enables robots to localize functional object components in 3D scenes. It is a challenging task that requires spatial understanding and task interpretation. Current open-vocabulary 3D segmentation methods primarily focus on object-level recognition, while scene-wide part segmentation methods attempt to segment the entire scene exhaustively, making them highly resource-intensive and time consuming. Balancing segmentation performance in terms of granularity, accuracy, and speed remains a challenge. As one step towards alleviating this, we introduce T-FunS3D, a task-driven hierarchical open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation method that provides actionable perception for robotic applications. Our method takes as input the 3D point cloud and posed RGB-D images of an indoor scene. We construct an open-vocabulary scene graph by extracting instances and their visual embeddings in the environment. Given a task description, T-FunS3D identifies the most relevant instances in the scene graph and locates their functional components leveraging a vision-language model. Experiments on the SceneFun3D dataset demonstrate that T-FunS3D is comparable to state-of-the-art in open-vocabulary 3D functionality segmentation, while achieving faster runtime and reduced memory usage.

</details>


### [59] [Unveiling the Unknown: Open Vocabulary Object Detection with Scene Graphs](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05916)
*Yi Chen,Yinghao Lu,Zhehao Li,Chenchen Yan,Jiafei Wu,Chong Wang,Jiangbo Qian*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a framework for open-vocabulary object detection that enhances performance by incorporating structured relationships and scene graphs to model interactions and spatial arrangements between objects.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: There is a need to improve the detection of novel object categories by considering structured, image-specific relationships that are often missed in existing approaches.

Method: The proposed Scene-guided Relational Modeling framework uses scene graphs to capture semantic and spatial relationships among objects, incorporates a Relation Attention Module, and includes a scene-based textual alignment branch for knowledge distillation.

Result: The model demonstrates superior performance in detecting novel categories, outperforming other open-vocabulary object detection methods and achieving improved Average Precision (AP) on COCO and LVIS datasets.

Conclusion: The integration of visual relations with semantic information through the proposed framework leads to better detection outcomes for novel object categories.

Abstract: Open-vocabulary object detection seeks to identify novel object categories that were not part of the training data. Many knowledge distillation-based approaches have shown promising performance by transferring knowledge from pre-trained vision-language models to object detection. However, these methods often overlook structured, image-specific relationships between objects, such as interactions and spatial arrangements. This oversight can significantly restrict the effectiveness of detecting novel categories. To address this issue, we propose a Scene-guided Relational Modeling detection framework. This framework utilizes scene graphs to capture structured semantic and spatial relationships between candidate regions and their contextual objects. It explicitly models interactions among neighboring regions and incorporates a Relation Attention Module to implicitly amplify the key relational cues extracted from the scene graph. Furthermore, we present a scene-based textual alignment branch that distills category knowledge from captions to guide relational alignment. This approach facilitates a seamless integration of visual relations with semantic information for enhanced detection performance. Comprehensive experiments show that our model achieves superior performance compared to other OVOD methods, improving the AP for novel categories on COCO and LVIS datasets.

</details>


### [60] [Synthetic Data Generation and Vision-based Wrinkle and Keypoint Detection for Bimanual Cloth Manipulation](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.06292)
*Ariel Herrera,Xueyang Kang,Atal Anil Kumar*

Main category: cs.CV

TL;DR: This paper presents a novel framework for robotic manipulation of textiles using a synthetic data pipeline for training a wrinkle detection system, which combines CNNs and YOLOv8 for effective grasping point extraction.


<details>
  <summary>Details</summary>
Motivation: The study addresses the challenges in robotic manipulation of textiles caused by deformation and self-occlusions, which complicate visual perception and state estimation of cloth.

Method: A Blender-based synthetic data pipeline was developed to export auto-annotated keypoints, combined with manually labeled renders and real-world data to train a wrinkle detector. The perception framework employs a CNN for keypoint detection and a YOLOv8-OpenCV pipeline for grasping point extraction.

Result: The keypoint model achieved a Mean Position Error (MPE) of 1.7615 pixels and the perception system effectively transferred to real fabrics without fine-tuning, outperforming existing baselines under challenging conditions such as high occlusion and severe folds.

Conclusion: The proposed system shows significant improvements in robotic manipulation of textiles, demonstrating robustness in perception and accuracy in identifying keypoints for effective grasping and ironing of garments.

Abstract: Robotic manipulation of textiles remains challenging because continuous deformation and self-occlusions hinder the robust visual perception required to estimate the cloth's state. To address the lack of annotated real-world data, we developed a Blender-based synthetic pipeline exporting auto-annotated keypoints, and combined manually labeled renders with real-world data to train a wrinkle detector. We present a perception framework integrating a CNN for permutation-invariant keypoint detection and a YOLOv8-OpenCV pipeline to extract grasping points from structural wrinkles. A proposed bimanual algorithm uses this system to stretch fully folded garments via wrinkles, transitioning to keypoint-based ironing once corners emerge. The keypoint model achieves a Mean Position Error (MPE) of 1.7615 pixels. The perception system transfers to physical fabrics without fine-tuning, outperforming baselines that fail in high-occlusion states or yield false positives on severe folds.

</details>


### [61] [MemoryCard: Topic-Aware Multi-Modal Clue Compression for Long-Video Question Answering](https://arxiv.org/abs/2606.05917)
*Qing Yang,Pengcheng Huang,Xinze Li,Zhenghao Liu,Yukun Yan,Yu Gu,Ge Yu,Gang Li,Maosong Sun*

Main category: cs.CV
